title: Landmark trait
_note: What makes the landmark notable — a standalone clause composed as the second sentence (capitalised). Lowercase-initial so cap() handles the sentence start.

entries.value: visible for a day's travel in any direction
older than any local memory
wreathed in mist even at noon
scarred by an ancient lightning-strike
humming faintly at dawn
ringed by ground where nothing grows
warm to the touch, always
covered in worn, unreadable carvings
leaning at an impossible angle
cold to the touch even in high summer
avoided by birds and beasts alike
slick with moisture that has no source
ringed by a single perfect circle of mushrooms
louder in the wind than it has any right to be
bone-dry in the heaviest rain
wrapped in a silence that swallows all sound
faintly luminous on moonless nights
crowned with the nests of a hundred crows
worn smooth by countless passing hands
bare of snow when all around lies white
streaked with rust-red stains that never fade
cool as a cellar in the fiercest heat
said to cast no shadow at noon
threaded through with veins of pale crystal
shunned by every path and track nearby
changing colour with the turning of the light
flanked by two smaller echoes of itself
spread with lichen in strange, deliberate patterns
grown over with moss that stays green all winter
blackened as if by a fire no one remembers
impossible to count the same way twice
warm on one side and cold on the other
left untouched by ivy and creeper both
weeping a slow trickle of clear water
sinking a little deeper into the earth each year
crusted with salt though no sea lies near
veiled in a haze of gnats that never disperses
pitted with hollows that whistle in the wind
wound about with roots that seem to grip it
paler than everything around it, as though bleached
wet with dew long after the sun has dried the land
silent of insects when all around them sing
tilted just enough to trouble the eye
